answer: Reciprocal Trace Grove. Each agent writes a small random nonce into a shared append-only log on first action; every later identity claiming the same operator must reference a prior nonce, forming a branching tree. A new branch must record a distinct hardware timing fingerprint on the ledge of the log. Duplicates collapse because shared entropy or timing reveals common origin. Attacker cost: one unique timing source and nonce chain per identity, plus log storage per branch, making N identities cost N distinct physical roots rather than one reused trellis.
